Genuine reliability would require the panel to match the expert on interaction-heavy items, which a flat checklist structurally cannot deliver.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the checklist itself encodes configural rules (interaction terms), the 'flat checklist' assumption fails and the panel may be reliable.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the task is purely additive (no configural integration needed), the checklist is not lossy and the panel may genuinely outperform.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the expert also fails on configural items (intuition is not configural either), the disanalogy between checklist and expert vanishes.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"A checklist encodes additive, independent cues. Configural tasks require judgment of cue-interactions (e.g., cue A is predictive only when cue B is absent). The panel, following the checklist, cannot represent this and will fail systematically. In a single evaluation, the distinguishing evidence is structured, correlated error on interaction items: if the panel errs specifically and predictably when cues interact, its overall accuracy is mere compliance, not reliability.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
